title: What a database transaction protects
subtitle: Keep related changes from half-succeeding
learning_objective: Explain why related writes should be grouped in a transaction.

scenes.title: THE HALF-TRANSFER
scenes.body: Money leaves account A, then a second update fails before account B receives it.

scenes.title: Group one logical operation
scenes.body: A transaction lets multiple database statements succeed together or roll back together, subject to the database's transaction semantics.

scenes.title: Transaction shape
Important boundary
scenes.body: A database transaction cannot automatically roll back an external email, payment provider call, or message already sent. Those need separate reliability patterns.

scenes.question: If the second database statement fails before commit, what should the transaction do?
scenes.explanation: The application should roll back the transaction so the logical operation does not leave only the first change committed.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Use a transaction for related database changes that must preserve one consistent outcome.
